verdict.rationale: Logseq's own docs describe an official Logseq Sync service. It syncs graphs between Desktop, Android and iOS, and each graph is end-to-end encrypted with a user password using Age and ChaCha20-Poly1305, with both file contents and names encrypted. Coverage is held at partial because the docs cap sync at 10 graphs, and hands-on users report the sync as buggy and not yet reliable, though not as failing to work. Missing for 10: independent confirmation that the vendor cannot read synced data (key custody is not explicitly documented), evidence of reliable, bug-free sync in practice, and sync beyond the 10-graph limit.

support.subject: As a power-user, an official sync service keeps my notes updated across all my devices with end-to-end encryption the vendor can't read

citations.quote: Syncs up to 10 graphs between Logseq Desktop, Android, and iOS.
Yes, your graph is end-to-end encrypted.
Each graph is encrypted with a password. The contents of the file as well as its name are all encrypted.
